http://groups.google.com/group/rhipe/browse_thread/thread/ba41b4b4d5c574a6/47cd3c7495395f25?q=stand
,because the person had my exact initial error message. Saptarshi
advised them to reinstall from the package instead of the git source.
His initial problem went away at that point, so I followed the same
advice. I installed from a downloaded .gz instead of building from
the git repository and my problem went away (I also required the use
of the mapred.job.tracker='local' argument, but that isn't enough to
get my build to work.) Everything looks nice now. If anyone is
searching this out at some date in the future: use the package zips
before attempting to build the package zips.

Though the new question is how to build the package from the source.
It seems like both me and that initial person were missing something
in order to build from the git repository source.

Mystery solved!

The git source isn't up to date. If you download the latest package
then git the latest source you will discover the main.cc files are
different. Replacing the main.cc from the latest package direct
download in the git repository download corrects the problem. All
adds up now.

start tinkering!

Jeremiah

Hi,

You did download Rhipe from the website [1] ?
Also, the following worked for me:

map <- expression({
lapply(map.values,function(seed){
set.seed(seed)
numDraws <- 1e2
r <- .5 #radius... in case the unit circle is too boring
x <- runif(numDraws, min=-r, max=r)
y <- runif(numDraws, min=-r, max=r)
inCircle <- ifelse( (x^2 + y^2)^.5 < r , 1, 0)
rhcollect(1,sum(inCircle) / length(inCircle) * 4)
})
})

z <- rhmr(map, ofolder="/tmp/test", inout=c('lapply','sequence'),
N=10,mapred=list(mapred.reduce.tasks=0,mapred.job.tracker='local'),jobname='test')

rhex(z)
